about: measure contests of 2024 in Maine, in the layout of plan/PLAN.md section 3 with the fields data/README.md adds (D3). Built by pipeline/local_medsl.py from pipeline/intake/medsl_precinct.py's cache.

medsl.name: MIT Election Data and Science Lab, Precinct-Level Returns 2024 by Individual State, Harvard Dataverse doi:10.7910/DVN/NYTPDU, version 1.0
medsl.note: precinct returns compiled by MEDSL from each state's official sources (named per state in its README); added up to the contest by pipeline/intake/medsl_precinct.py, files 2024-me-precinct-general.csv

model.name: the model's own forecast, method D3-v1.1
model.note: each year forecast from a fit on earlier years only; no polls are used

nara.name: National Archives, Electoral College Results (the sitting president's party)
nara.licence: US federal public record; no licence printed

klarner.name: Carl Klarner, State Legislative Election Returns, 1967-2022, Harvard Dataverse doi:10.7910/DVN/FJOGJB, v1.0, released 2024-06-12T21:56:14Z (the races route (a) is fitted on)

notes: counted by county: MEDSL's wording of a local question does not show which place holds it, so a question held across several counties appears once per county

p.not_computed: a local measure: its threshold is the one state law sets for its kind of measure, which the source's wording does not show, and the place that holds it is not shown either (it is counted by county); not inferred (the orchestrator, 2026-11-07 06:16)

source.name: Maine Legislature, Senate Advance Journal and Calendar, December 4, 2024 (S.C. 3): communication of December 2, 2024 from Secretary of State Shenna Bellows, 'a summary of the results of the November 5, 2024, Referendum Election'. The Secretary of State's own pages (maine.gov/sos) were refused (403).

ballot_text.source_title: Question 1: Citizen Initiative (the source gives only the kind, no title)

fact.why: The source lists the November 5, 2024 Referendum Election as five singly numbered questions with no '1A/1B' pairs; it gives only each question's kind and vote counts, not its wording or whether any question is a competing measure. Q1 is the only citizen initiative in the list, but the only other non-bond question is Q5, 'State Referendum', which this document does not describe, so I cannot tell from it whether Q5 is a legislative competing measure to Q1. The Citizen's Guide (maine.gov/sos) that would settle it was refused twice. Left null.

source.name: Maine Legislature, Senate Advance Journal and Calendar, December 4, 2024 (S.C. 3): communication of December 2, 2024 from Secretary of State Shenna Bellows, 'a summary of the results of the November 5, 2024, Referendum Election'. p.not_computed: Me. Const. art. IV, pt. 3, §18(2) sets another threshold for an initiative with a competing measure on the same ballot, and the source does not show whether this measure is one; its ballot text, read in step (a), does not show it either (data/measure/ballot-texts.json)

ballot_text.source_title: Question 2: Bond Issue (the source gives only the kind, no title)

fact.why: The source lists the November 5, 2024 Referendum Election as five singly numbered questions with no '1A/1B' pairs; it gives only each question's kind and vote counts, not its wording or whether any question is a competing measure. The Secretary of State labels Q2 a bond issue, not a citizen initiative, so it is not an initiative with a competing measure. Inferred from that label; the Citizen's Guide (refused) was not read.

threshold.rule: 2/3 of both houses, then ratified by majority of electors voting thereon
threshold.quote: by proper enactment ratified by a majority of the electors voting thereon at a general or special election, the Legislature may authorize the issuance of bonds on behalf of the State
threshold.matched: by the type the ballot text states (bond; data/measure/ballot-texts.json)

p.under: the model's own (D3-v1.1), like past measures
p.note: this route's back-test of statewide measures shows more near-even finishes than it forecast (12 against 9.1 within 1 point of ½, and 11 against 6.9 within 20,000 votes, 2018 to 2024), so p may be low
